title: Pumpkin and feta fritters with lamb chops

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a whole food or a plain staple (pumpkin, feta, eggs, cornflour, lamb chops, Greek yoghurt), with no jars, stock pots or packet mixes.

supermarket.reason: Every item is stocked at Tesco, and although eight lamb chops is a bit pricier than mince, it is still an everyday purchase.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a grater, a bowl and a frying pan, and shallow-frying fritters and chops is well within a confident beginner's skills.

works.reason: 600g grated pumpkin bound with 2 eggs and 4 tbsp cornflour makes a sensible fritter batch for four, and with two chops each and the stated frying times it should all come out cooked and golden.

honest_times.reason: Peeling and grating the pumpkin plus batch-frying the fritters and chops in one pan fits roughly within the 45 minutes printed, which suits a standard pace.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed item, including the cumin, mint, lemon and salad leaves, appears in the steps, and nothing unlisted is used.

seasonal_feel.reason: Pumpkin fritters are the centre of the plate in late October, the week of Halloween, with the lamb as a partner rather than overshadowing them.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are plain, brief British English that a neighbour could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Vegetable fritters, lamb, a yoghurt sauce and leaves make a proper, appealing meal of real food.
